issues.title: Undo and redo accepted edits inside an active sketch
issues.body:
## Problem and result
Undo currently addresses committed document features while an active sketch stores disposable edits. Make accepted sketch operations undoable without changing unrelated committed document history.

## Scope
One bounded sketch-session journal for accepted entity, constraint, dimension and annotation edits through the existing authoritative commands. A pending pointer/inline preview is not an accepted edit. Native shortcuts, toolbar actions and control API share dispatch and inspection. Finish remains one document edit; Cancel discards the entire draft.

## Acceptance criteria
- Within an active sketch, Undo/Redo restores accepted draft states, stable IDs, inferred references, geometry and presentation. Rejected solves and hover do not add journal entries.
- Undo never mutates unrelated committed features while the sketch is active. A new accepted edit after Undo drops the draft redo branch.
- Finish commits the resulting draft once; document Undo restores the previous sketch/solid state. Cancel preserves the pre-session document and its journal.
- Explicitly define behavior for a pending line point or inline value before traversing accepted draft history; preserve user work.

## Proposed verification and evidence
Create a snapped closed outline, undo and redo the last segment, then add/edit a dimension and undo/redo it. Verify relation IDs, profile closure and visible cue/session state. Finish, document Undo/Redo, re-enter/Cancel and save/reopen. Use one real-app workflow plus native shortcut dispatch; do not replace this with mock history tests.

## Public reference evidence
- Reference keyboard shortcuts (reference `keys`) — retrieved 2026-10-11.
- Sketch workflows (reference `sketch`) — retrieved 2026-10-11.
Research exact active-command behavior in permitted public examples before claiming compatibility. Session journal architecture and acceptance are Alloy requirements.

## Limits and open questions
Newly identified foundation gap; no draft-history support is claimed by the current snapping slice. Exact pending-input precedence needs a bounded public behavior record. This does not introduce a second authoritative document model or persistent global command log.
